'''Campbell''': {{legend0|#ffc8cd|30–40%}} {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Wally Hickel]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Tony Knowles (politician)|Tony Knowles]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Alaska sidebar}} The '''1994 Alaska gubernatorial election''' took place on November 8, 1994, for the post of [[List of Governors of Alaska|Governor]] of [[Alaska]], United States. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate [[Tony Knowles (politician)|Tony Knowles]] narrowly defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] candidate Jim Campbell and [[List of Lieutenant Governors of Alaska|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Jack Coghill]] of the [[Alaskan Independence Party]]. This was the only governorship to flip from Republican to Democratic in the 1994 [[Republican Revolution]]. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominated==== * [[Tony Knowles (politician)|Tony Knowles]], former mayor of [[Anchorage, Alaska|Anchorage]] (1982–1987) ====Eliminated in primary==== * Sam Cotten, former speaker of the [[Alaska House of Representatives]] (1989–1991) * [[Steve McAlpine]], former [[Lieutenant Governor of Alaska|lieutenant governor of Alaska]] (1982–1990) ===Results=== {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results{{cite book |last1=Barone |first1=Michael |last2=Ujifusa |first2=Grant |title=The Almanac of American Politics 1998 |publisher=National Journal Inc. |location=Washington, D.C. |isbn=0-89234-080-0 |page=82}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Tony Knowles (politician)|Tony Knowles]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 24,727 | percentage = 44.07% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Steve McAlpine]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 17,482 | percentage = 31.16% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Sam Cotten | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 13,899 | percentage = 24.77% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 56,108 | percentage = }} {{Election box end}} ==Other candidates== [[Incumbent]] Governor [[Wally Hickel]] had been elected as the candidate of the Alaskan Independence Party in the [[1990 Alaska gubernatorial election|1990 gubernatorial election]]. In April 1994 he rejoined the Republican Party and announced in August that he would not stand for re-election.{{cite news| url = https://www.nytimes.com/1994/08/25/us/two-in-the-house-advance-in-drive-for-senator-s-seat.html | title = Two in the House Advance In Drive for Senator's Seat | access-date = 2008-07-23 | date = 1994-08-25 | work=[[The New York Times]]}} For the Republican nomination, businessman Jim Campbell narrowly defeated another former mayor of [[Anchorage, Alaska|Anchorage]], [[Tom Fink]]. Lieutenant Governor Jack Coghill was easily selected as the candidate for the Alaskan Independence Party while [[Jim Sykes]] ran for the [[Green Party of Alaska]]. Ralph Winterrowd, an Anchorage businessman, ran as the candidate of the Patriot Party.{{Cite news |last=Pagano |first=Rosanne |date=1994-11-03 |title=Ad Wars Break Out In Governor's Race |page=5 |newspaper=Daily Sitka Sentinel |location=Sitka, Alaska |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/104269681/ad-wars-break-out-in-governors-race/ |access-date=2022-06-23 |via=Newspapers.com}} ==Campaign== Both main candidates in the election were regarded as moderates and favored oil exploration in the [[Arctic National Wildlife Refuge]] as well as cuts in the state budget.{{cite web| url = https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19941023/1937490/alaska-democratic-candidate-has-been-having-bad-hair-days | title = Alaska Democratic Candidate Has Been Having Bad Hair Days | access-date = 2008-07-24 | date = 1994-10-23 | work=[[The Seattle Times]]}} [[Opinion poll|Poll]]s near the election showed Knowles with a strong lead over Campbell. During the election the Campbell campaign ran an advertisement comparing Knowles's hair with President [[Bill Clinton]]'s. The advert was criticised by supporters of Knowles who felt it implied that he was a [[womanizing|womanizer]].{{cite news| url = https://www.nytimes.com/1994/11/09/us/the-1994-elections-state-bt-state-west.html | title = THE 1994 ELECTIONS: STATE BT STATE; West | access-date = 2008-07-24 | date = 1994-11-09 | work=[[The New York Times]]}} ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" ! width="110px" | Source ! width="80px" | Date ! width="100px" | Knowles (D) ! width="100px" | Campbell (R) |- | Dittman Research | Nov. 3, 1994 | '''44%''' | 33% |} ==Recount== As the results were counted state officials said that the contest between Knowles and Campbell was too close to call, with Knowles having a small lead.{{cite news| url = https://www.nytimes.com/1994/11/16/us/democrat-gets-nearer-top-job-in-maryland.html | title = Democrat Gets Nearer Top Job In Maryland | access-date = 2008-07-24 | date = 1994-11-16 | work=[[The New York Times]] | first=Michael | last=Janofsky}} Knowles declared victory on November 18 after the official count showed that he was ahead by 528 votes with only 217 votes remaining to be counted.{{cite news| url = https://www.nytimes.com/1994/11/20/us/democrat-declares-victory-in-alaska.html | title = Democrat Declares Victory in Alaska | access-date = 2008-07-24 | date = 1994-11-20 | work=[[The New York Times]]}} He described the victory as the "largest margin I think I've ever won by" as his Anchorage mayoral election wins had always been by very narrow margins. Campbell contested the results and called for a recount, which was paid for by the state as the candidates were within half a percent of each other.{{cite web| url = https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19941122/1943212/democrat-takes-alaska-governorship | title = Democrat Takes Alaska Governorship | access-date = 2008-07-24 | date = 1994-11-22 | work=[[The Seattle Times]]}} Campbell also wanted to look into some voter incentives that had taken place including [[raffle]]s and free gasoline for voters. These were defended as attempts to increase [[Voter turnout|turnout]] and had been authorised by election officials.{{cite web| url = https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19941204/1945201/voter-incentives-raise-questions----apparent-loser-in-alaska-governors-race-cries-foul | title = `Voter Incentives' Raise Questions -- Apparent Loser In Alaska Governor's Race Cries Foul | access-date = 2008-07-24 | date = 1994-12-04 | work=[[The Seattle Times]]}} The initial count showed Knowles with 87,701 votes and Campbell with 87,118 votes. The results of the recount slightly narrowed the gap between them with Knowles ending at 87,693 and Campbell at 87,157.{{cite web |url=http://www.elections.state.ak.us/result94.htm |title=1994 GENERAL ELECTION OFFICIAL RESULTS STATEWIDE SUMMARY |access-date=2008-07-24 |publisher=Alaska Division of Elections |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080716200806/http://www.elections.state.ak.us/result94.htm |archive-date=2008-07-16 |url-status=dead }} Knowles's victory margin was the smallest in any Alaska gubernatorial election.{{cite web| url = https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19941204/1945202/democrat-wins-in-alaska-recount----republican-wont-pursue-voter-incentive-complaints | title =
